about.text: Sweet whey concentrated and spray-dried to a powder, still holding its lactose, proteins and minerals. Used in bakery, soups and other processed foods, and in animal feed.

links.name: Tetra Pak Dairy Processing Handbook, ch. Milk and whey powder

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Whey is mostly water, so it is evaporated first and then dried. The key step is lactose crystallisation before drying; without it the powder is a hygroscopic lump. The handbook gives no dryer temperatures.

links.name: Tetra Pak Dairy Processing Handbook, ch. 18 Milk and whey fractionation

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: Cooled or pasteurised first so it does not ferment.
Flash-cooled to start lactose crystals, then held in crystallisers.
Spray-dried (drum drying exists, with bran as filler to ease scraping).
